summary.headline: Q4 FY26 presales hit record INR2,632 crores (+89% QoQ), but FY26 reported PAT was a loss of INR872 crores on revenue-recognition timing and merger accounting.
summary.overview: Embassy Developments posted record Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores and FY26 presales of INR4,631 crores (+128% YoY), with 93% of the INR5,000 crore guidance achieved. FY26 collections were INR1,673 crores, slightly below FY25's INR1,852 crores, which management attributed to the lag from H2-weighted presales. Reported FY26 revenue fell to INR1,732 crores and PAT swung to a loss of INR872 crores, which management framed as structural (completion-based revenue recognition and reverse-merger fair value step-up). FY27 guidance is INR6,000 crores own presales (plus INR2,000 crores from DM projects), INR3,000 crores collections and about INR19,400 crores of new launch GDV. Two legal overhangs (CIRP petition and KIADB resumption order) were resolved, and the ASM framework exit took effect 6 May 2026.

segments.name: Embassy Citadel (South Mumbai, Worli)
segments.commentary: Launched mid-February 2026 with 1 million sq ft and GDV over INR8,800 crores; prelaunch of INR797 crores in roughly 45 days, about 8% of inventory absorbed. Excavation underway.

segments.name: Embassy Verde Phase 2 (Embassy Springs)
segments.commentary: 87% absorbed in Q4, generating Q4 presales of INR588 crores. Citadel plus Verde Phase 2 contributed about INR1,385 crores, or roughly 53% of Q4 presales.

segments.name: Bangalore luxury (Embassy Eden and others)
segments.commentary: INR10 crore-plus ticket launches accounted for over 65% of FY26 Bangalore sales in that segment, roughly INR2,000 crores. Embassy Eden is 49% sold with target OC in FY31.

segments.name: OC-received portfolio
segments.commentary: 98% sold, with FY26 presales of INR573 crores and collections of INR645 crores from this portfolio.

segments.name: Development management (DM) projects
segments.commentary: Juhu (ultra-luxury) and Sky Terraces in Bangalore, combined GDV about INR6,000 crores; revenue is recognised as fee income over construction, not on OC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 own presales guidance INR6,000 crores (about 30% YoY), plus INR2,000 crores from DM projects, total INR8,000 crores.
FY27 collections guidance about INR3,000 crores (about 75% YoY); construction spend planned about INR2,500 crores.
FY27 new launch GDV about INR19,400 crores: 9 owned projects of INR13,300 crores plus DM projects; another source cites 11 owned projects.
Net debt to equity to be kept at 0.5x or less; net debt roughly flat in FY27 and progressive reduction from FY28; debt paydown over about 24 months.
Cost of debt about 14.8% currently, targeted to fall to about 10% gradually over 12 to 18 months.
Net surplus margin expected close to 50% over the next several years; management declined to give an EBITDA margin range or revenue guidance.
capex_capacity: Construction spend in FY26 was INR1,182 crores, about 71% of collections. Embassy Citadel total project spend is about INR3,000 crores, leaving INR5,000-6,000 crores plus of surplus, per management.
Embassy Citadel contractor is La Tim (described by management as a notch above L&T). OC application submitted for 109 Phase 1 in Gurgaon; partial OC received for Golf City, Savroli Phase 1.

Project progress: Paradiso 100% sold, 80% complete, OC FY27; East Avenue 94% sold, 73% complete, OC FY28; Verde 90% sold, 17% complete, OC FY29; Edge 74% sold, 66% complete, OC FY28; Park Panvel 74% sold, 41% complete, OC FY28-FY30; Greenshore 63% sold, 8% complete, OC FY31.

Launch timing: One North Tower (Bengaluru, INR1,400 crores GDV) in Q1 FY27 after building plan approval; Knowledge Park (INR4,500 crores) end of Q1 or spilling to Q2; Sky Terraces end Q1 or Q2; Juhu in Q2; Springs Front Parcel Q2 or Q3. Whitefield JDA (INR2,000 crores, 68.5% share) and Hebbal Plot A (INR2,100 crores, 91% share) are also in the FY27 pipeline.

Planned pipeline beyond FY27 of 20.4 million sq ft and GDV about INR23,500 crores, plus a 3,250-acre fully paid land bank. Nashik SEZ land is under a stay from MIDC, with next hearing on 12 June; debonding is targeted within FY27.
demand_pricing: Unsold inventory including Worli is about INR12,000 crores GDV, or about INR10,000 crores excluding the commercial asset. Management expects INR2,000 crores of FY27 presales from existing stock (Citadel about INR1,000 crores) and INR4,000 crores from new launches.
Presales over the last quarters: INR198 crores in Q1, INR409 crores in Q2, INR1,392 crores in Q3, INR2,632 crores in Q4. Over 80% of FY26 presales came in H2.
FY26 presales of INR4,058 crores equal 27.5% of unsold inventory value of INR14,728 crores (about 18% of launched and ongoing GDV, per a correction on the call).

Management says it is not yet seeing a market slowdown, and it expects to gain share in a consolidating market. It also expects costs to rise and to pass them on through pricing. Citadel is priced below top Worli developers, and management is not ruling out discounts.
Management said the stock was below fair value and that the promoter and Blackstone shareholder debt of about INR1,100-1,121 crores would be converted to equity later, once the share price recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timelines for the large projects (Knowledge Park, Whitefield, Springs, One North Tower)?
qa_highlights.answer: One North Tower is to launch in Q1 FY27. Knowledge Park is due at the end of Q1 or in Q2. Juhu is Q2, Sky Terraces end-Q1 or Q2, and Springs Front Parcel Q2 or Q3. Most launches fall in H1 or early H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Citadel's RERA completion date moved from 2032 to 2035?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a RERA buffer for a large tower, with the target at FY31-32. It also said this is in line with market norms for 300-metre towers.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt and leverage move given FY27 collections of about INR3,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction spend of about INR2,500 crores is planned, so debt will not fall much in FY27. Net debt to equity is to stay at or below 0.5x, with about 0.3x comfortable, and progressive reduction from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give an EBITDA range. It shifted to net surplus margin, which it expects to be close to 50% over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was about INR550 crores of interest expensed rather than capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said whatever could be capitalised was. The rest relates to OC-received projects and corporate expenses, and some borrowing funded premium approval charges for Blu.

qa_highlights.question: Interest and promoter pledge: is the pledge being reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledge rose from about 47% to 68% when the share price fell, with no new debt taken. It expects a return to about 48% and full unpledging over 2 to 3 years.

risks_watch: Reported losses (FY26 PAT -INR872 crores, EBITDA -INR300 crores) persist until OCs arrive from FY28, with no revenue guidance.
Cost of debt about 14.8% and gross institutional debt about INR4,100 crores; reduction depends on collections and refinancing.
FY27 presales of INR6,000 crores require about 2.2x the FY26 Q4 run rate for the full year, and a Q1 launch cluster (One North, Knowledge Park, Sky Terraces) must deliver.
Lam Research 25-acre sub-lease sits on a KIADB lease ending June 2029; management expects a routine extension.
Nashik SEZ MIDC dispute: next hearing 12 June 2026; debonding expected in FY27.
Shareholder debt of about INR1,100 crores (Blackstone) and promoter pledge (68% of promoter shares at peak) are overhangs.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on presales momentum, legal wins and the FY27 pipeline. Evasive on EBITDA, revenue and specific cost-of-debt and dilution timing, and it shifted the focus to net surplus margin and collections.
key_quotes: Q4 FY '26 was the strongest quarter in our company's history.
Our reported P&L for FY '26 reflects an accounting loss of INR872 crores at the PAT level.
We want to keep our net debt levels to 0.5x or less.
And we expect that to be close to 50% over the course of the next several years as these projects get delivered.
The presales to collection conversion is a structural lag and not an operational issue.
